2608.00446.title: Structured Proxy Features for Multimodal NSCLC Survival Prediction from Pretreatment CT
2608.00446.paper_summary: Lung cancer results in roughly 1.8 million fatalities annually worldwide, with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) comprising the majority of cases. Despite advancements in treatment, survival stratification remains challenging due to intratumoral heterogeneity inadequately captured by conventional descriptors. Standard radiomic and deep learning techniques regard imaging features as independent quantities, overlooking structured interactions between tumor characteristics. We evaluate whether structured proxy features can enhance multimodal NSCLC survival prediction by augmenting pretreatment computed tomography (CT) representations, radiomics, and clinical variables with six simulation-derived features designed to capture interactions between heterogeneity and morphology. A radiomic-parameterized cellular automaton generates growth-rate and necrosis-ratio proxy features from baseline CT by using entropy and sphericity to compute low-dimensional proxy parameters. The imaging backbone is a Transformer-based Masked Autoencoder (TMAE), which was chosen after a systematic evaluation with alternative encoders within the same pipeline and provides attention-based visualizations that highlight tumor regions receiving higher model attention. On the public Lung1 cohort (n = 390), the primary four-modality fusion attained a C-index of 0.641 (iAUC 0.731, log-rank p < 0.001). The primary result compares favorably with prior multimodal results on Lung1 (C-index 0.631; iAUC 0.592 [15]) under a comparable evaluation protocol, while a separate exploratory coefficient-optimization analysis achieved a best observed C-index of 0.662 (iAUC 0.748). These results indicate that, in addition to conventional radiomic, deep, and clinical representations within the Lung1 benchmark, simulation-derived proxy features may provide complementary predictive information within this fixed Lung1 benchmark.
2608.00446.paper_summary_zh: 肺癌每年在全球造成約180萬人死亡，其中非小細胞肺癌（NSCLC）佔大多數病例。儘管治療有所進步，生存分層仍然具有挑戰性，因為腫瘤內部異質性未能被傳統描述方法充分捕捉。標準的放射組學和深度學習技術將影像特徵視為獨立的量，忽略了腫瘤特徵之間的結構性互動。我們評估結構性代理特徵是否能通過增強治療前的計算機斷層掃描（CT）表徵、放射組學和臨床變數來改善多模態NSCLC生存預測，這些特徵是由六個模擬衍生的特徵設計的，旨在捕捉異質性與形態之間的互動。一個以放射組學參數化的細胞自動機通過使用熵和球形度從基線CT生成生長速率和壞死比率的代理特徵，以計算低維代理參數。影像基礎架構是一種基於Transformer的遮罩自編碼器（TMAE），經過系統評估後選擇了該編碼器，並提供基於注意力的可視化，突顯出接受模型更高注意力的腫瘤區域。在公共的Lung1隊列（n = 390）中，主要的四模態融合達到了C指數0.641（iAUC 0.731，log-rank p < 0.001）。主要結果與Lung1的先前多模態結果相比表現良好（C指數0.631；iAUC 0.592 [15]），在可比較的評估協議下，而一項單獨的探索性係數優化分析達到了最佳觀察C指數0.662（iAUC 0.748）。這些結果表明，除了在Lung1基準內的傳統放射組學、深度和臨床表徵外，模擬衍生的代理特徵可能在這一固定的Lung1基準內提供互補的預測信息。
